reviews.decision_reason: select_demand admits every corpus row because the predicate is demand_score >= 3 and all supplied records have scores 3 through 9. Under the strict demand criteria, several selected records are not independently supported by observed job/pain/trigger/outcome evidence in the supplied package. The boundary therefore over-selects before the later normalization truncation hides the issue.

normalize collapses the selected demand table to head(len([0])), which keeps only the first row. That makes the final output deterministic but by positional truncation rather than by supported demand evidence, and it can mask the upstream over-selection while discarding other records without market-demand justification visible in the package.

assemble_provenance receives the already-normalized one-row needs table and deterministically emits matching provenance with record_id, source_id, source_weight, and rank. The supplied handoff hashes show the evidence_sources artifact was preserved for the downstream job; no local defect is visible in this boundary.
